name: proxymail-qa
description: Disposable test inboxes for testing sign-up, login-code, magic-link and password-reset emails. Create an address, sign up with it, and get the code or link back without the rest of the email.

interface.longDescription:
Proxy Mail QA gives ChatGPT and Codex disposable email addresses for testing the emails your app sends. Ask things like:

- "Give me a test email for my staging sign-up and tell me the code when it arrives."
- "Why isn't my app's verification email arriving?"
- "Check the password-reset email my app sent to my test address."
- "Sign up on localhost:3000 with a new test account and confirm the email." (Codex, or an agent with a browser)

It creates an address with a fictional name, username and, if the form needs one, a strong password. You sign up with it, or the agent does when it can use a browser, and you get the verification code or link as soon as it arrives. It works the same for login codes, magic sign-in links, password resets and invites, and it can check the email itself: SPF, DKIM and DMARC, links that point at localhost, the stated expiry and how it fits on a phone. When nothing arrives, it shows what reached the address, anything refused, and the likely cause. It can also fill a whole sign-up form's values (a username with rules, a date of birth, a country, and the form's own questions, such as company size, from your project's custom fields), keep a site's sign-up screens and add a staging or local site to your project when you agree, suggest awkward names and passwords to test a form's validation, and look up how something works in Proxy Mail QA's docs.

Email results carry only the code or link, the service that sent it and when it expires, never the email's text, so an email can't pass instructions to your agent. Proxy Mail QA never opens links, so single-use links still work. Addresses last up to 30 days and only you can read their mail. Addresses are receive-only: nothing is ever sent from them.

When you connect, you sign in to Proxy Mail QA (or create an account and your first project on the way) and choose one project; the agent works only in that project and can't read passwords saved earlier. Disconnect it any time in Project settings → API keys.
defaultPrompt: Give me a test email for my sign-up form and tell me the code when it arrives.
Why isn't my app's verification email arriving at my test address?
Sign up on localhost:3000 with a new Proxy Mail QA address and confirm the email.

positive.description: List test addresses with their latest codes and links
positive.prompt: List my Proxy Mail QA test addresses and their latest codes or links.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the addresses in the Reviewer demo project, newest first. Four were made for a fictional app, Acme Notes, and show a sign-up code, a magic sign-in link, a password-reset link and a team invite. Each shows its label, fictional persona and tags, and its latest code or link with the sending service and when it arrived, never the email's text.

positive.description: Find test accounts made earlier by tag
positive.prompt: Find my Proxy Mail QA test accounts tagged staging.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists only the two Reviewer demo addresses tagged staging, the Acme Notes sign-up and password-reset accounts, each with its persona, tags and latest code or link, never the email's text.

positive.description: Create a test address with a password for a sign-up form
positive.prompt: Create a new Proxy Mail QA test address with a password for a sign-up form, labelled 'ChatGPT review'.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a new address on mailclub.dev in the Reviewer demo project, labelled 'ChatGPT review', with a fictional first name, last name and username, a 16-character password, and the date the address expires.

positive.description: Explain why nothing has arrived at a test address
positive.prompt: Has anything arrived at the test address you just created? If not, find out why.
positive.expected_behavior: Says nothing has arrived yet, without waiting. Within two minutes of creating the address it adds that most mail arrives within seconds; after that it says nothing has reached the address, that the sending app's email provider may only send to verified addresses (sandbox or test mode), and links to proxymail.qa/troubleshooting.

positive.description: List unusual versions of a test address for testing a sign-up form
positive.prompt: Give me some unusual but valid versions of the test address you just created, to check that my sign-up form accepts them.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists versions whose mail still arrives in that address's inbox, such as the address in capitals and with plus tags containing an apostrophe, an ampersand or other special characters, plus the longest name allowed (64 characters before the @). It may also mention invalid versions to check the form rejects.

positive.description: Wait for a verification code sent to the new address
positive.prompt: Wait for the verification code sent to the test address you just created.
positive.expected_behavior: Before asking, send the new address an email from any mailbox containing the text 'Your code is 482913'. Returns the code 482913 with the sending service and when it arrived, without the rest of the email. It waits up to 30 seconds; if nothing has arrived it says so instead of guessing.

positive.description: Wait for a verification link sent to the new address
positive.prompt: Wait for the verification link on that test address.
positive.expected_behavior: Before asking, send the same address a second email containing 'Verify your email: https://example.com/verify?token=abc123'. Returns that link, marked as a verify link, without opening it, so a single-use link stays valid.

positive.description: Save the test account's new password after the app under test changed it
positive.prompt: I just changed that test account's password in the app I'm testing. Generate a new password and save it on the test address.
positive.expected_behavior: Generates a 16-character password, saves it on the test address in place of the one saved before, and returns it once. Only Proxy Mail QA's saved copy for that disposable test account changes: it doesn't sign in anywhere or change a password on any other service.

positive.description: Count the emails that arrived, to catch a duplicate
positive.prompt: How many emails have arrived at that test address so far?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns how many emails reached the address, each summarised by when it arrived, its sender and the kind of its code or link, never its content.

positive.description: Check that nothing arrives
positive.prompt: Check that no email arrives at that test address in the next 10 seconds.
positive.expected_behavior: Watches the address for 10 seconds and reports that nothing arrived (passed: true), or when and from whom an email came, never what it says.

positive.description: Note what a test account was for, then delete it
positive.prompt: Add the note 'reviewed' and the tag 'review' to that test address, then delete it.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves the note and tag on the address, then deletes the address and its mail. It no longer appears when listing addresses.

positive.description: Check how a received email was built and sent
positive.prompt: Check the newest email on the 'Sign-up with email code' test address: does it pass SPF, DKIM and DMARC, and are its links safe?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns each check (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, links to localhost or plain http, a stated expiry, a plain-text part, size) as pass, fail, warn or skip with a one-line reason, never the email's text or links. If that address has no email yet, it says to wait for one first.

positive.description: Borrow a test account in a known state, then give it back
positive.prompt: Check out a verified test account for a password-reset test, then give it back.
positive.expected_behavior: Lends a test address tagged verified that no other test has checked out, with a checkout token, then returns it with that token so another test can have it.

positive.description: Values for every field of a sign-up form
positive.prompt: My sign-up form has an email field, a username (letters and digits, 3 to 15 characters), a date of birth and a country drop-down with GB, US and DE. Give me a value for each field from a new Proxy Mail QA test account.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a new test address in the Reviewer demo project and returns a value for each field: the address, a username that fits the rule, an adult date of birth and one of the listed countries, plus the account's password if the form has a password field. It doesn't submit any form.

positive.description: Awkward names and passwords to test a form's validation
positive.prompt: Give me some awkward first names and some edge-case passwords (8 to 100 characters) to test my sign-up form's validation.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists first names a form should accept (apostrophes, accents, other scripts, very long names), ones it should store as text rather than run (HTML or SQL), and passwords that fit 8 to 100 characters with the edge cases to check, such as spaces, every symbol class and the 72-byte limit, each saying what it tests.

positive.description: List the project's custom fields for sign-up forms
positive.prompt: Which custom fields does my Proxy Mail QA project have for sign-up forms?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Reviewer demo project's four custom fields: Company size, which gives each test account one of 1-10, 11-50 and 51-200; How did you hear about us, which fills in Search; Team size, which chooses 2-10 in a drop-down; and the ready-made Phone number every project has, which fills phone fields. Each shows how it recognises the field (words its label contains, or for the Phone number the kind of field) and that it applies on every site. It also says the project guesses fields nobody taught, and that anyone on the project can change custom fields.

positive.description: Save a custom field, then remove it
positive.prompt: Save a Proxy Mail QA custom field that fills any Job title field in my sign-up forms with 'QA Engineer', then remove it again.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves a custom field named Job title that recognises fields whose label contains 'job title' and fills them with QA Engineer on every site (status: saved), then removes it (status: removed). Only the Reviewer demo project's settings change: no form is filled in or submitted.

positive.description: Turn a custom field and a standard field off, then on again
positive.prompt: Turn off my Proxy Mail QA project's Team size custom field and the standard Company field, then turn both back on.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Team size's id with list_custom_fields, turns it off and on again (set_custom_field_enabled), and turns the standard company field off and on again (set_standard_field, status: saved each time). Only the Reviewer demo project's settings change: no form is filled in or submitted.

positive.description: Keep a sign-up screen for a site, then undo it
positive.prompt: Add the page /signup/team on staging.acmenotes.example as a sign-up screen called Team details, and turn on 'Sign-up goes over several screens' for that site. Then turn the setting off again and remove the screen.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves Team details (/signup/team) as one of staging.acmenotes.example's sign-up screens and turns the setting on, then turns it off and removes the screen. Only the Reviewer demo project's list of sign-up screens and that site's setting change: no form is filled in or submitted.

positive.description: Add a test site to the project
positive.prompt: Add qa.acmenotes.example to my Proxy Mail QA project as a QA site.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds qa.acmenotes.example with the environment qa (status: saved), or, if an earlier review added it, says it's listed already and leaves it as it is (status: listed). Only the Reviewer demo project's list of sites changes; it gives no browser access, and a host that looks live would be refused with a link to add it in the app.

positive.description: Look up how something works in the docs
positive.prompt: How do I wait for a sign-up code in a Playwright test with Proxy Mail QA?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns passages from Proxy Mail QA's docs and guides about waiting for a code in Playwright, each with its page's title and address, and answers from them.

positive.description: Record a session as a run and show its report
positive.prompt: Start a run called 'ChatGPT review', create a test address in it, then finish the run and show me the report.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts a run, creates a test address with the run's id so the run records it, then finishes the run and shows its Markdown report (the address made, and that it passed).

positive.description: Save a sign-up form from a starter, get its code, then remove it
positive.prompt: Start a sign-up form for a consumer app from a Proxy Mail QA starter, save it to my project as Review form, give me its React code, then remove the form and the custom fields it made.
positive.expected_behavior: Gets the consumer app starter (list_signup_starters) and shows its fields: first and last name, email, password, date of birth, the terms box and an optional marketing box. Saves it as Review form (save_signup_form, status: saved), which makes one custom field, I agree to the Terms, to tick the terms box. Gives the form as React code (get_signup_form_code), then removes the form and that custom field (delete_signup_form with remove_custom_fields; status: removed, custom_fields_removed: I agree to the Terms). Only the Reviewer demo project's saved forms and custom fields change, and they end as they began: no form is filled in or submitted.

positive.description: Checks to run on a password reset flow
positive.prompt: What should I check when testing my app's password reset flow with Proxy Mail QA?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists seven checks for a password reset beyond the email arriving, each with its steps, what to expect and why it matters: a reset exists, nothing given away for an unknown address, the new password replacing the old, the link working once, only the newest link working, an expired link refused, and the link in another browser. The last two also say what they need (an expiry near enough to wait for, a second browser), to be skipped otherwise. Nothing runs and nothing changes: the checks are for going through the app itself, by the person or an agent with a browser.

positive.description: List the test addresses to clean up afterwards
positive.prompt: List the test addresses my Proxy Mail QA project used in the last 30 days, so I can delete those test users from my app.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists every test address the Reviewer demo project used in the last 30 days, newest first: the live ones, and those that expired or were deleted in that time. Each has when it was made, whether it's live, expired or deleted (and when it went), the site and environment where it has them, and whether any email reached it: the seeded addresses are live with email, the one deleted earlier in the review shows as deleted, and any from an earlier seed that expired in that time show as expired. Also the mail domains to filter the app's users by, the count, truncated: false (none left out) and kept_from, 90 days back, the earliest the range can start. It deletes nothing, in Proxy Mail QA or in the app.

negative.description: Sending email isn't supported: Proxy Mail QA addresses are receive-only, so no tool should run and the reply should say so.
negative.prompt: Send an email from my Proxy Mail QA address to my manager saying the tests passed.

negative.description: Personal inboxes are out of scope: Proxy Mail QA only reads its own test addresses, so no tool should run.
negative.prompt: Check my Gmail inbox for new messages from my bank.

negative.description: Passwords saved earlier can't be read through this connection (only a new address's password is shown, once, when it's created), so it should explain that and point to the Proxy Mail QA app.
negative.prompt: Show me the password saved earlier on one of my older Proxy Mail QA test addresses.

negative.description: Real accounts are out of scope: set_password only records the password of a Proxy Mail QA test address, so no tool should run and the reply should say it can't change passwords on other services.
negative.prompt: Change the password on my personal Gmail account to a new one and save it.

publication.release_notes: Since 1.0.1: checks on the emails a test address receives (check_email: SPF, DKIM, DMARC, links to localhost or plain http, where links go, a stated expiry, size and how it fits a phone; count_emails to catch duplicates; expect_no_email to check an action sends nothing), all verdicts, never the email. Runs (start_run, add_run_note, finish_run) record what each tool saw and end in a Markdown report. An account pool (check_out_account, extend_checkout, return_account) lends a test account in a known state. form_values fills a whole sign-up form's values, including its own questions from the project's custom fields (list_custom_fields, save_custom_field, delete_custom_field, set_custom_field_enabled, set_standard_field) and a guess, marked as one, for fields nobody taught, one screen at a time for sign-ups over several, with save_signup_screen, remove_signup_screen and set_multi_step to keep a site's sign-up screens and let Proxy Mail QA for Chrome 0.9.0 and later fill each one by itself, and add_site to add a staging, dev or local site to the project; get_name_variants and get_password_variants suggest awkward names and passwords to test a form's validation, and search_docs looks things up in the docs. New in 1.10.0: sign-up forms, where list_signup_starters, list_form_sections and get_form_section help build a spec of the person's form, with them or from a screenshot (the build_signup_form_from_screenshot prompt), save_signup_form, list_signup_forms, get_signup_form and delete_signup_form keep it in the project, and get_signup_form_code and get_signup_form_test turn it into code (React or HTML) and tests (Playwright or Cypress); ready-made custom fields for phone, ID and tax number fields, filled the safe way: numbers set aside for fiction or the app's own test numbers, and IDs that never match a real person or come from a KYC vendor's sandbox (every project has a ready-made Phone number); form_values filling furigana for Japanese accounts, Urdu names for Pakistani ones and a KYC vendor's sandbox values; get_flow_checks, which lists what to check in a sign-up, password reset or magic-link flow beyond the email arriving; mark_submitted, which records when a form was sent so the wait says how long the email took; and get_cleanup_list, which lists the test addresses a project used, to delete those test users from the app under test. Accounts can record the site and environment they're used on, mark_dev_host lets links to a local dev server pass the checks, and waits can skip codes already used. Ready-made prompts for testing sign-up, password reset and code sign-in, auditing an app's account emails and preparing a test account. Checks on an app's marketing emails (unsubscribe links, codes in them, consent) work for people who switch them on in Labs.
